pharm: A recombinant urate-oxidase enzyme that converts uric acid to soluble allantoin, used to manage or prevent tumour-lysis-associated hyperuricaemia
quick: 0.2 mg/kg IV once daily over 30 minutes for up to 5 days
Limited data; use only if clearly needed
Unknown if excreted in milk; caution/avoid during use
Not relevant to short IV course
Uric acid (chilled sample handling), G6PD status, hemolysis/methemoglobinemia, anaphylaxis
summary: Rasburicase is a recombinant urate-oxidase enzyme used for the initial management of elevated plasma uric acid in patients with leukaemia, lymphoma and solid tumours receiving anticancer therapy expected to cause tumour lysis and significant hyperuricaemia. It enzymatically converts poorly soluble uric acid to highly soluble allantoin, rapidly lowering uric acid. The usual dose is 0.2 mg/kg IV once daily over 30 minutes for up to 5 days. It carries a BOXED WARNING for anaphylaxis, hemolysis (it is CONTRAINDICATED in G6PD deficiency, which must be screened in at-risk patients), methemoglobinemia, and interference with uric acid measurements (blood must be collected into pre-chilled heparin tubes and kept on ice, then assayed within 4 hours, because rasburicase continues to degrade uric acid ex vivo). Treatment is discontinued immediately and permanently for serious hemolysis, methemoglobinemia or anaphylaxis.
indications: Initial management of plasma uric acid levels in adult and paediatric patients with leukaemia, lymphoma and solid-tumour malignancies receiving anticancer therapy expected to result in tumour lysis and subsequent elevation of plasma uric acid

dosage.d: 0.2 mg/kg as a single daily dose
dosage.t: Intravenous infusion over 30 minutes, once daily for up to 5 days
dosage.n: Dosing beyond 5 days or more than one course is not recommended

dosage.d: Reconstitute and dilute to a final volume of 50 mL in 0.9% sodium chloride; do NOT use filters or bolus/IV-push
dosage.t: Infuse over 30 minutes through a separate line (or flush line before/after if shared)
dosage.n: Do not shake; discard unused portion

admin: Give as a 30-minute intravenous infusion; do not administer as a bolus
Do not use an in-line filter and do not co-administer with other drugs through the same line without flushing
Screen patients at higher risk (those of African or Mediterranean ancestry) for G6PD deficiency before starting; it is contraindicated in G6PD deficiency
For uric acid monitoring, collect blood into pre-chilled tubes containing heparin, keep on ice, and assay within 4 hours to avoid falsely low results
Have measures for anaphylaxis available; discontinue immediately and permanently for serious hypersensitivity, hemolysis or methemoglobinemia
moa: Rasburicase is a recombinant form of urate oxidase (uricase), an enzyme absent in humans. It catalyses the enzymatic oxidation of uric acid into allantoin, which is far more water-soluble and readily excreted by the kidneys. By lowering existing uric acid (rather than merely preventing its formation as allopurinol does), it rapidly reduces the uric-acid load that can precipitate in renal tubules and cause acute uric-acid nephropathy during tumour lysis. The hydrogen peroxide produced as a by-product of the reaction can cause oxidative hemolysis and methemoglobinemia, particularly in patients with G6PD deficiency.

absolute: History of anaphylaxis or severe hypersensitivity to rasburicase
History of hemolytic reactions or methemoglobinemia with rasburicase
relative: Patients at higher risk of G6PD deficiency who have not yet been screened
monitor: Signs of hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis during and after infusion
Plasma uric acid using correct chilled-sample technique

preg: There are limited human data on rasburicase in pregnancy. It should be used during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is not known whether rasburicase is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions and the short treatment course, caution is advised and breastfeeding may need to be temporarily withheld.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is defined for renal impairment; rasburicase is used precisely to prevent uric-acid nephropathy. Monitor renal function as part of tumour-lysis management.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is defined for hepatic impairment.

moderate: No clinically significant pharmacokinetic drug interactions established (rasburicase is an enzyme cleared by peptide degradation)
interactions.alcohol: Not relevant to a short intravenous course
interactions.diagnostics: Rasburicase enzymatically degrades uric acid at room temperature in collected blood, causing falsely LOW uric-acid readings - collect into pre-chilled heparin tubes, keep on ice and assay within 4 hours

rare: Hypotension and chest pain during infusion
emergency: Methemoglobinemia with cyanosis and hypoxia unresponsive to oxygen

monitoring: Plasma uric acid using pre-chilled heparin tubes on ice, assayed within 4 hours
Haemoglobin and hemolysis markers (especially first dose)
Pulse oximetry/methemoglobin level if cyanosis or unexplained hypoxia
Vital signs and signs of hypersensitivity during and after infusion
Renal function and electrolytes as part of tumour-lysis-syndrome management
counsel: This medicine is given by a drip to control high uric acid during cancer treatment
Tell your team at once if you feel breathless, develop a rash, swelling, dizziness or chest tightness during the infusion
You may be tested for an enzyme deficiency (G6PD) before treatment because this drug can break down red blood cells in people who lack it
Report unusual tiredness, dark urine or bluish skin/lips, which can signal blood problems
Blood samples for uric acid must be handled in a special way (kept cold), so timing of tests is important
pk: Plasma uric acid falls rapidly, often within about 4 hours of the first dose
Enzyme exposure increases with dose; uric-acid lowering is prompt
Sustained uric-acid control over the daily-dosing course (up to 5 days)
Store refrigerated (2-8 C), protect from light; do not freeze; do not shake reconstituted solution
pearls: BOXED WARNING: anaphylaxis, hemolysis, methemoglobinemia, and interference with uric-acid measurements
CONTRAINDICATED in G6PD deficiency - screen high-risk patients (African/Mediterranean ancestry) before use
Discontinue immediately and permanently for serious hypersensitivity, hemolysis or methemoglobinemia
Falsely low uric-acid results occur unless blood is drawn into pre-chilled heparin tubes, kept on ice and assayed within 4 hours
Unlike allopurinol, it enzymatically destroys existing uric acid (to soluble allantoin), giving rapid reduction
Hydrogen peroxide by-product drives the oxidative hemolysis/methemoglobinemia risk
missed: Rasburicase is administered by healthcare professionals on a fixed daily schedule during inpatient cancer care, so patients do not self-manage doses. The care team will give each dose at the scheduled time.
overdose: There is no reported specific overdose syndrome or antidote. Monitor closely for hemolysis and methemoglobinemia; manage methemoglobinemia supportively (methylene blue is generally avoided in G6PD-deficient patients) and provide oxygen, transfusion and exchange transfusion as needed for severe hemolysis. Discontinue the drug.
